heading: Yili 2 · Shi Hun Li 士昏禮 · The Marriage of an Ordinary Officer (Steele, chapters III-IV) · Shi Hun Li II.6 · The Presentation of Vegetables … The Feast, when the Parents4n-Law are Dead

items.text: Three months after marriage, offer vegetables in the ancestral temple to the spirit of your deceased father-in-law.
items.quote: three months after the event the bride goes to the ancestral temple and offers vegetables
items.conflict: Bible forbids offerings to the dead (Deut 26:14; Ps 106:28).

items.text: Three months after marriage, offer vegetables in the ancestral temple to the spirit of your deceased mother-in-law.
items.quote: takes another basket of vegetables, with which she enters the room... announces herself to her noble mother-in-law
items.conflict: Bible forbids offerings to the dead (Deut 26:14; Ps 106:28).

items.text: Feast the men and women of the bride's escort as your deceased parents would have done.
items.quote: The feasting of the men and women of the bride's escort is done by the bridegroom with the same ceremony as his father and mother would have used.

items.text: Treat the bride to must in the chamber, as her parents-in-law would have done.
items.quote: an old servant of the family treats the bride to must in the chamber, facing south, and using the same ceremonial as the parents would have used if they were alive.

work: The Marriage of an Ordinary Officer, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Cer
heading: Yili 2 · Shi Hun Li 士昏禮 · The Marriage of an Ordinary Officer (Steele, chapters III-IV) · Shi Hun Li I.8 · The Meeting in Person … The Digestif

items.text: Present the wild goose to her father and bow twice to the ground, honoring him as you receive his daughter.
items.quote: carrying a wild goose... lays down the goose and kowtows twice

items.text: Receive the bridegroom with bows and invitations, yielding precedence as to an honored guest.
items.quote: meets the bridegroom outside the gate... bows twice... invites him with a salute to enter... yieldings of precedence

items.text: Prepare a mat and resting place for the ancestor's spirit in the ancestral temple to witness the marriage.
items.quote: lays a mat to the west of the door of the room of his ancestral temple for the spirit of the ancestor
items.conflict: Deut 18:10-12; worship belongs to God alone.

items.text: Salute one another, share the marriage feast and cups, and bow together in mutual respect.
items.quote: the bridegroom salutes the bride... both make their offerings... The husband and wife both bow in reply

items.text: Follow him to his house, mount the carriage he has brought, and enter as his wife.
items.quote: the bride following down the west steps... she takes hold and mounts the carriage herself

items.text: Prepare the wedding feast, wash the vessels, and serve the food and drink as directed.
items.quote: The assistants remove the cover of the wine-jar... Those who carry the tripods wash their hands... lay the meat on the stands

items.text: Offer the first portion of the relishes, millets, and lung to the ancestors before eating.
items.quote: both make their offerings of the relishes, the two kinds of millet, and the lung
items.conflict: Deut 18:10-12; worship belongs to God alone.

work: The Marriage of an Ordinary Officer, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Cer
heading: Yili 2 · Shi Hun Li 士昏禮 · The Marriage of an Ordinary Officer (Steele, chapters III-IV) · Shi Hun Li I.1 · Sending the Present … Laying out the Vessels and Meats

items.text: Send a wild goose to the father of the girl to make known your intentions.
items.quote: In making known his intentions to the father of the girl, the father of the young man sends a wild goose.
items.needs_role: Father of the young man; father of the girl

items.text: Spread a mat for the ancestral spirit and place a body-rest before receiving a marriage proposal.
items.quote: The girl's father spreads a mat for the ancestral spirit to the west of the door ... and at the right end of the mat he places a body-rest.
items.needs_role: Father of the girl; ancestors of the girl's family

items.text: Send a messenger with a wild goose to ask the girl's name, and let the girl's father consent.
items.quote: The messenger, holding a goose in his hands, requests permission to be allowed to ask the girl's name, and the host, through the usher, consents.
items.needs_role: Father of the young man; father of the girl

items.text: Meet the messenger at the door, bow, and entertain him with food and drink as a guest.
items.quote: The host, dressed like the messenger, goes to meet him outside the door, and bows twice.
items.needs_role: Father of the girl; messenger from the young man's family

items.text: Make an offering of dried flesh and hash and pour a libation as a sacrifice.
items.quote: The guest ... makes an offering of the dried flesh and hash, and thereafter pours a libation with the ladle.
items.needs_role: Guest/messenger; ancestral spirits of the host family

items.text: When the divination is favorable, send a wild goose to announce the result.
items.quote: In announcing the favourable result of the divination, a wild goose is presented.
items.needs_role: Father of the young man; father of the girl

items.text: Send a bundle of black and red silks and a pair of deer-skins to complete the preliminaries.
items.quote: The presents sent by the father of the young man to complete the preliminaries are a bundle of black and red silks and a pair of deer-skins.
items.needs_role: Father of the young man; father of the girl

items.text: Send a wild goose to ask the time for the ceremony; the girl's father should decline to name a time but accept the divined day.
items.quote: A wild goose is sent by the messenger who goes to ask of the girl's father the time for the ceremony. He declines to name a time ... announces the day which has already been discovered by divination.
items.needs_role: Father of the young man; father of the girl

items.text: See that the wedding vessels, foods, and wine are prepared for the ceremony.
items.quote: the assistants place three tripods outside the door of the bridegroom's private apartments
items.needs_role: Father of the young man; the bridegroom

work: The Marriage of an Ordinary Officer, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Cer
heading: Yili 2 · Shi Hun Li 士昏禮 · The Marriage of an Ordinary Officer (Steele, chapters III-IV) · Shi Hun Li II.8 · Sixteen Notes

items.text: Obey your father's command to marry, so that he may fulfil his duties in the ancestral temple.
items.quote: Go meet your helpmeet, and so enable me to fulfil my duties in the ancestral temple.

items.text: Be diligent in taking the lead as husband, but with respectful consideration, for she is the successor of your mother.
items.quote: Be diligent in taking the lead as husband, but with respectful consideration, for she is the successor of your mother.

items.text: Be careful and reverent. Day in day out disobey no command of your new parents.
items.quote: Be careful and reverent. Day in day out disobey no command of your new parents.

items.text: Be diligent and reverent. Day in day out disobey no rule of the household.
items.quote: Be diligent and reverent. Day in day out disobey no rule of the household.

items.text: Reverently regard what your parents said to you; observe what they told you; day in day out let there be no fault with you.
items.quote: Reverently regard what they said to you. Observe what they told you. Day in day out let there be no fault to find with you.

items.text: If you did not fetch your bride in person, go to her parents after three months and ask for an interview.
items.quote: I, who have already secured this alliance without coming to the house, now ask for an interview.

items.text: When you visit your wife's parents, lay down a pheasant as a present and bow twice.
items.quote: lays down the pheasant which he has brought as a present. Then, bowing twice, he goes out.

items.text: When your mother-in-law bows to you, reply with a bow.
items.quote: the lady bows once, and he replies. She bows a second time, and he goes away.

items.text: Invite your son-in-law to drink and have your wife serve the relishes when he visits.
items.quote: invites the son-in-law to drink must... the mother-in-law serves the relishes.

items.text: When your son-in-law departs, take leave of him with two bows.
items.quote: takes leave of him with two bows.

work: The Marriage of an Ordinary Officer, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Cer
heading: Yili 2 · Shi Hun Li 士昏禮 · The Marriage of an Ordinary Officer (Steele, chapters III-IV) · Shi Hun Li I.12 · The Completion of the Marriage Ceremony … The Entertainment of the Escort

items.text: Offer the traditional gifts of dates and chestnuts to your father-in-law and dried meat to your mother-in-law when you first meet them.
items.quote: the bride takes a basket of dates and chestnuts... lays the basket before the mat

items.text: Offer the bride the cup of must as a sign of welcome and acceptance.
items.quote: The parents-in-law then help the bride to must.

items.text: Wash your hands and set the meal before your parents-in-law.
items.quote: the daughter-in-law washes her hands and presents food to them.

items.text: Assist your parents-in-law in their offering before the meal.
items.quote: The bride assists the parents-in-law at their offering before eating
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with worship of God alone.

items.text: Do not make your daughter-in-law eat food you have touched; provide fresh sauce for her.
items.quote: the father-in-law declines to allow it, and sets down fresh sauce, because the other had been soiled by his fingers.

items.text: Offer the bride a cup to settle her meal after she has eaten.
items.quote: her mother-in-law offers her a digestif

items.text: Host a feast for the bride to honor her as a new member of the household.
items.quote: The father- and mother-in-law unite in giving a feast to the bride

items.text: Step down from the host's place and let the bride take the eastern steps, handing over to her the position of mistress of the household.
items.quote: descend before the bride by the western steps... the bride thereafter descends by the eastern steps, assuming the position they have demitted.

items.text: Send the stand and remaining meat back to the bride's family as a token of continued bond.
items.quote: The stand used by the bride is sent back to her people, with the remaining meat on it.

work: The Marriage of an Ordinary Officer, from The I-li, or Book of Etiquette and Cer
heading: Yili 2 · Shi Hun Li 士昏禮 · The Marriage of an Ordinary Officer (Steele, chapters III-IV) · Shi Hun Li II.8 · Sixteen Notes

items.text: Have your daughter taught deportment and handiwork for three months before her marriage.
items.quote: she is taught deportment and handiwork for three months

items.text: Pledge your daughter with must in the chamber, and then await the bridegroom's coming.
items.quote: The father pledges his daughter with must in the chamber, and then awaits the bridegroom's coming

items.text: Admonish your daughter to preserve her integrity of character as she leaves.
items.quote: admonishes her that she shall preserve her integrity of character

items.text: Admonish your daughter concerning her clothes and hairpin as she prepares to go.
items.quote: As to her clothes and hairpin, her mother, standing at the head of the western steps, admonishes her with regard to these.

items.text: Bring on the relishes for the bride at her feasting.
items.quote: the mother-in-law brings on the relishes

items.text: Offer the cup to the bride at her feasting.
items.quote: the cup is offered by the father-in-law

items.text: When you toast your father-in-law, change the cup and yourself bring the relishes.
items.quote: she changes the cup, and herself brings forward the relishes

items.text: Do not treat your father-in-law as an equal: do not accompany him or bow when he washes a cup for you.
items.quote: does not dare to accompany her father-in-law down the steps

items.text: Do not take part in the sacrifices of your husband's house until you have been three months in it.
items.quote: It is not until she has been three months in her husband's house that a woman may take part in sacrifices.

items.text: If you are the wife of a son by a concubine, do not offer food to your parents-in-law.
items.quote: she does not offer food to her parents-in-law
items.conflict: Concubinage is a violation of the one-flesh union; favoritism among sons is sin.

items.text: Before your son marries, submit the proposed bride's name to divination.
items.quote: my master is about to submit the name to divination
items.conflict: Divination is forbidden; trust God's will, not omens (Deut 18:10-12).
